content.value_statement: Paid campaigns need many clear variants without unsupported claims or weak landing-page alignment. This skill creates structured ad copy and angle matrices that match the destination page and format requirements.
actual_capabilities: Generates RSA headlines and descriptions for a specified offer and destination page.
Builds angle matrices with distinct hooks for creative testing.
Adapts copy to the selected platform, format, audience, and brand voice.
Checks each unit against destination-page claims for message match.
Flags unsupported, restricted, or policy-sensitive claims for review.
Prepares a handoff-ready creative set after user-approved saving.
limitations: It does not upload, activate, or manage advertising campaigns.
It needs a destination URL to verify message match.
It cannot verify legal, platform, or regional policy compliance conclusively.
It relies on user-provided exports and page content for performance context.

use_cases.title: Prepare Google Search ads
use_cases.description: Create RSA headlines and descriptions that reflect a landing-page offer and fit the requested format.

use_cases.title: Plan paid social tests
use_cases.description: Build a matrix of angles and hooks to organize creative experiments for a new campaign.

use_cases.title: Refresh underperforming copy
use_cases.description: Preserve winning themes while proposing new message-matched variants for weak ads.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic RSA copy
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate 15 RSA headlines and 4 descriptions for [offer]. The destination page is [URL]. Use a [brand voice] tone.

prompt_templates.title: Build a testing matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 3 by 3 angle matrix for [offer] on [platform]. Match every hook to [landing page URL] and identify the echoed claim.

prompt_templates.title: Revise existing ads
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these ad variants: [paste]. Keep the strongest themes, replace weak variants, and maintain message match to [URL].

prompt_templates.title: Run a claims-aware draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Create [format] ads for [offer] and [audience]. Use only these approved claims: [claims]. Flag any claim that needs evidence or policy review.

output_examples.input: Generate RSA copy for a meal-planning service with a weekly trial.
output: A set of RSA headlines and descriptions within the selected format limits.
Each unit identifies the landing-page claim it matches.
Any unsupported price or guarantee claim is flagged for review.

output_examples.input: Build creative tests for a project-management tool.
output: Three distinct angles, such as time savings, team visibility, and planning clarity.
Three hooks per angle with message-match notes for the destination page.

best_practices: Provide the offer, destination URL, audience, platform, and desired ad format.
Supply approved claims and brand guidance before requesting publish-ready copy.
Review flagged claims and policy risks before using creative in a campaign.
anti_patterns: Do not request claims, prices, guarantees, or testimonials without supporting evidence.
Do not use output as a substitute for platform policy or legal review.
Do not omit the destination URL when message match is required.

faq.question: Which ad formats can this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports RSA copy, hooks, and angle matrices. Provide the platform and format so it can apply relevant limits.

faq.question: Does it publish ads to an account?
faq.answer: No. It produces creative and does not upload, activate, or manage campaigns.

faq.question: Why is a destination URL needed?
faq.answer: The URL provides the claim and value proposition that the ad copy should match.

faq.question: Can it use existing performance data?
faq.answer: Yes. You can provide a manual export of existing creative and performance data for context.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertain claims?
faq.answer: It flags them for evidence or policy review instead of presenting them as approved claims.

faq.question: Can it create competitor ad copy?
faq.answer: It can study observed competitor angles and formats, but it should not copy competitor creative.
